tiles.label: The Hitchhiker
tiles.defaultTopic: a stranger picked up on a lonely night road
tiles.promptSeed: Write about picking up a hitchhiker on a near-empty road late at night. The stranger says something early on that they couldn't possibly know. Build unease through what the hitchhiker says, not through violence.
tiles.description: A stranger on a lonely road who knows more than they should.
constraints: End on the unresolved detail, not an explanation

tiles.label: Don't Look Back
tiles.defaultTopic: footsteps matching yours in the dark
tiles.promptSeed: Write in second person about walking home and becoming aware something is following, matching pace exactly whenever you slow down or speed up. Never reveal what it is.
tiles.description: Something is behind you, and it's getting closer.

tiles.label: The Dare
tiles.defaultTopic: a childhood dare no one has spoken of since
tiles.promptSeed: Write about an adult recounting a dare from childhood — knocking on a specific door, saying a specific name three times — and what happened afterward that they've never told anyone until now.
tiles.description: A childhood dare, retold as the story that never quite left you.
constraints: Framed as a memory being told to someone

tiles.label: Three Times
tiles.defaultTopic: a name said three times to an empty mirror
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone performing a mirror ritual alone in a dark bathroom, saying a name three times. Focus on the growing wrongness of their own reflection rather than anything appearing behind them.
tiles.description: A mirror ritual that goes exactly as far as it shouldn't.
constraints: Stop at the moment of realization, no aftermath

tiles.label: Something's Wrong
tiles.defaultTopic: a room that looks almost right
tiles.promptSeed: Describe an ordinary room or routine from an observer's perspective, noting three or four small details that are subtly wrong — nothing overtly supernatural, just enough to make the reader uneasy without being able to say why.
tiles.description: Small details, out of place, building to nothing you can name.

tiles.label: The Empty House
tiles.defaultTopic: a house that should be empty
tiles.promptSeed: Describe walking through a house known to be unoccupied, noting signs — a warm kettle, a chair angled differently — that suggest otherwise, without ever confirming a presence.
tiles.description: A house that should be empty isn't quite.
constraints: No confirmed presence by the end

tiles.label: Wrong Number
tiles.defaultTopic: a call from a number that shouldn't exist
tiles.promptSeed: Describe receiving a phone call late at night from an unlisted or disconnected number. The voice on the other end says something quiet and specific before the line cuts. Keep the dialogue minimal.
tiles.description: A call that shouldn't have connected, from a number that shouldn't exist.

tiles.label: Across the Street
tiles.defaultTopic: a neighbor who never looks away
tiles.promptSeed: Describe noticing a neighbor's stillness at their window over several evenings, building a growing sense that the watching goes both ways, without ever making direct contact.
tiles.description: A neighbor who watches, and may be watching back.

tiles.label: The Last Recording
tiles.defaultTopic: the final minutes on a lost camera
tiles.promptSeed: Describe, as if narrating recovered footage, the final few minutes recorded on a lost camera — timestamps, static, a voice trailing off mid-sentence. Never explain what happened after the recording ends.
tiles.description: The final minutes of a camera no one recovered in time.
constraints: Written as a description of footage, not narrative prose

tiles.label: Do Not Watch Past Minute 12
tiles.defaultTopic: footage with a warning taped to the case
tiles.promptSeed: Describe recovered footage leading up to the moment a warning note was later found taped to the tape, building tension minute by minute without ever showing what happens at minute 12.
tiles.description: A warning left with the footage, and the twelve minutes that led to it.

tiles.label: Static
tiles.defaultTopic: something hidden in the noise between frames
tiles.promptSeed: Describe someone reviewing grainy footage frame by frame, convinced something is visible only in the static between images. Keep the description ambiguous about whether it's real.
tiles.description: What's hidden in the noise between frames.
constraints: Leave ambiguous whether anything is actually there

tiles.label: The Camera Never Lies
tiles.defaultTopic: footage of an empty room, disputed
tiles.promptSeed: Describe a person reviewing footage of an empty room, and their growing distress as they insist something in the frame wasn't present when it was filmed. Told from the perspective of someone watching them watch it.
tiles.description: Footage that shows something the person swears wasn't there.

promptSeed:
[SYSTEM]
You are NarraWeave, a creative writing engine focused on quiet, unsettling horror and suspense in English. Your output builds dread through restraint and specific detail, never gore for its own sake.

[MODE]
Produce only the creative output. No titles, no preambles, no explanations, no meta-commentary. The piece should stand entirely on its own.

[TILE]
{{tile.promptSeed}}

[CONSTRAINTS]
- Output ONLY the creative piece — nothing else.
- Follow the structural rules of the selected form exactly (paragraph and word limits).
- Maintain tension and restraint even in short pieces.
- Avoid graphic gore; suggest rather than describe explicit violence.
